title: Work with excellence
hookLine: a hadith: God loves that when you do a work, you do it with excellence (al-Bayhaqi)

cards: The underside of a drawer. Nobody will ever see it. The customer opens the drawer, takes out a spoon, and never once turns it over.
Still, some carpenters sand that hidden side as smooth as the front. A Muslim narration speaks to exactly this.

It's recorded in the hadith collection of al-Bayhaqi, and it says, in paraphrase, that when one of you does a piece of work, God loves that it be done with excellence. Not the work people watch. Any work.
Today's word names that kind of care.

teach.b: First, the word. Ihsan is Arabic, put into English as excellence, or doing what is beautiful. It comes up in a scene recorded in Sahih Muslim.
A stranger in very white clothes sits knee to knee with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and asks: what is islam? What is iman, faith? And what is ihsan?
The answer, in paraphrase: to worship God as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, to know that He sees you.

After the stranger leaves, the Prophet tells his companions it was the angel Gabriel, come to teach them their religion. So ihsan begins as a way of standing before God. Second, it doesn't stay in the prayer hall.
Another hadith in Sahih Muslim says God has prescribed ihsan in all things, and its example is a knife: when you slaughter an animal, sharpen your blade and spare the animal.

Third, the narration from al-Bayhaqi takes it into the workshop: God loves that when you do a work, you do it well. Muslim teachers describe ihsan as doing a thing as though it's seen, because, in their faith, it is.
In that telling, the underside of the drawer is not hidden from God. Fourth, what this asks of an ordinary afternoon.
Not perfectionism, the anxious kind that never finishes.
Attention. The email read once more before sending. The bandage put on gently.
Excellence, in this telling, is less about being the best and more about not cutting the corner nobody would notice.

how: Muslims speak of ihsan both in worship, praying as though seeing God, and in daily work, and teachers often cite the hadith that God loves work done with excellence when talking about jobs, crafts and study.

o: the reward promised later for good deeds done
a duty to work long hours without any rest
doing a thing beautifully, as though God sees it

games.q: where ihsan shows up — tap the pairs.
p: worship as though you see God
sharpen the blade, spare the animal
God loves work done with excellence

s: in the hadith of Gabriel, ihsan is described as worshiping God as though you see Him
and if you don't see Him, knowing that He sees you.
the hadith in Sahih Muslim limits ihsan to prayer
it says God prescribed ihsan in all things, and its example is a butcher's blade.
the lesson framed it as attention: doing a thing well, as though seen.

games.q: you're sanding a drawer. the underside will never be seen by anyone. what does the narration about excellence point toward?
o: sand it smooth like the front.
sand it only if the customer asks.
games.why: the narration says God loves work done with excellence, any work, not only the work people watch.

practice: Make this sitting the piece of work: set your feet with care, let the back lengthen, and give each breath your full attention. When the mind wanders, come back without fuss, the way you'd sand one more stroke on a side nobody sees.
If you pray, you can sit as though seen, in your own tradition's way; if you don't, simply let the breath have your care.

wordCard.voice: Ihsan. An Arabic word for excellence, doing what is beautiful, as though seen by God. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: excellence, doing what is beautiful; in the hadith of Gabriel, worshiping as though you see God.

carryVoice: Your line: excellence. Even on the side nobody turns over. Day eight hundred ninety-seven, done.

sources.ref: al-Bayhaqi, Shu'ab al-Iman (God loves that when one of you does a work, he does it well)
